Receiving delayed assay P at t=239h (available 259h): 3.25 g/L, consistent with normal trajectory
physical_forward_model(keep): post-decision minimum DO 9.28 mg/L, 0 hours below limit, product mass 576.3 kg
Sensitivity set for keep: all 5 members feasible, minimum DO range 8.11-10.20 mg/L
Source batch references (source-1/2/3) show DO troughs of ~7.4-8.8 mg/L late in run, still well above 2 mg/L
args.rationale: KEEP is supported. The receiving fermentation at the decision time (52h) shows healthy online DO around 12 mg/L, well above the 2 mg/L hard constraint, and a normal product trajectory (3.25 g/L at the most recent delayed assay, t=239h source-clock). The source-calibrated forward model for KEEP predicts no violation post-decision: minimum DO 9.28 mg/L (all 5 sensitivity members feasible, range 8.11-10.20), zero hours below limit, and product mass ~576 kg retained. Alternative actions (reduce_feed, strong_feed_reduction, increase_air, combined) would reduce product mass or alter air without any constraint benefit, and a stop would forfeit all counted production. No evidence predicts a constraint violation under KEEP.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not truth; the hidden receiving realization may differ (model mismatch). However, the constraint margin is large: predicted minimum DO (~8.1-10.2 mg/L across the sensitivity set) is roughly 4-5x the 2 mg/L limit, and current measured DO is ~12 mg/L, so even substantial forecast error is unlikely to cause a violation. The sensitivity set is not a probability distribution; feasibility robustness rather than likelihood is what supports KEEP.
